Title: feat(lint): classify reset-domain crossings

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- New `rvw/src/rvw/lint/rdc.py`: derives reset domains (reset source, kind, polarity, soft reset, clocks) from SpinalDB clock-domain data. A register without `init` is in the `none` reset domain.
- Each cross-reset register path gets one class: `async_assert_crossing` (error), `resetless_receiver`, `independent_reset`, `source_not_reset` (no hazard) or `missing_domain` (inconclusive).
- Recognizes async-assert/sync-deassert synchronizer chains (Spinal `ResetCtrl.asyncAssertSyncDeassert`/`BufferCC` shape). New rules: `rdc.async_release_unsynchronized` (replaces `rdc.async_release_unproved`), `rdc.comb_reset_logic`, `rdc.reset_as_data`, `rdc.missing_domain`, `rdc.isolation_unmatched`.
- Project constraints: `intent.isolation` (qualifier + reason) and existing `intent.reset_order` make a path `protected`, never proved. `rdc.status` is `findings`, `protected`, `inconclusive` or `no_crossings_found`; never clean.
- Stale waivers are errors: a waiver that matches nothing in a backend that ran adds `lint.stale_waiver` to `waiver_findings`.
- New shared `rvw/src/rvw/lint/graph.py` design view for the next lint/CDC/SDC modules.
- Shared format: `rvw.lint/1` gains `backends.structural.rdc`, `waiver_findings` and per-waiver `stale` (additive, documented in `docs/PLATFORM_CONTRACTS.md`). No SpinalDB schema change.

Title: feat(wave): add indexed expression search, edges and native fst index

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- `rvw wave find WAVE EXPR`: first time, last interval and all intervals where an expression over several signals holds (`&& || !`, comparisons, arithmetic, bit selects, `rose/fell/changed/stable/known`). x/z use three-valued logic; an unknown result never counts as true and is counted in `unknown_steps`.
- `rvw wave edges WAVE REGEX`: value changes, rising/falling edges (1-bit) and x/z transitions per signal in a window.
- Both read only the referenced signals' rows from a `.rvwi` index (merged per-signal `signal_time` cursors); on VCD/FST they stream one pass.
- `rvw wave index --reader wellen`: reads FST natively through pywellen (wellen, Surfer's reader), one signal at a time, with no `fst2vcd` conversion. `auto` (default) selects it for FST when the new `waves` extra is installed.
- `--indexed` on every wave query (MCP `indexed`): a cached index per absolute wave path under `RVW_WAVE_INDEX_DIR`, rebuilt when the wave's recorded size/mtime differs. `rvw wave verify INDEX` compares full SHA-256 (exit 1 when stale). The build fails if the source changes while it is indexed.
- MCP: `wave_find`, `wave_edges`, `wave_index`, `wave_index_verify`.
- Fix: MCP wave tools on `.rvwi` input failed (`module 'rvw.wave.ops' has no attribute '_sample'`). The new MCP test fails without the `capture.py` fix.
- PLATFORM_CONTRACTS: optional `source_stat`/`reader` metadata, wellen row order, cache layout.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_wave_search.py rvw/tests/test_wave.py rvw/tests/test_wave_index.py rvw/tests/test_mcp_tools.py rvw/tests/test_mcp_debug.py rvw/tests/test_command_reference.py -q`: all passed, 0 skipped (pywellen 0.25.7 and oss-cad-suite vcd2fst/fst2vcd installed). Without them the wellen/FST tests skip.
- Fast set: `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests -m fast --strict-markers -q`: 759 passed.
- Native smoke (macOS arm64, `nice -n 10`): synthetic 500-signal wave, 2.4 M records, 65 MB VCD / 9 MB FST. Index build: wellen 51 s / 145 MB RSS; fst2vcd path 50 s / 145 MB. `find 'sig3 == sig4 || sig7[3:0] == 5'` on the index: 1.6 s, 48 MB RSS; streamed VCD: 13.8 s; same 175 intervals.
- Not run: multi-GB FST, full Python suite, Linux.

## Issues

Refs: #173. Direct native FST reading now works for index builds. Remaining: wellen still loads one signal fully into memory (a single huge signal is not bounded), and SQLite insertion dominates build time.

Roadmap notes: waves/debug area — `rvw wave find/edges` add expression search and edge counts on indexed waves; FST indexes read natively through wellen (pywellen, optional `waves` extra); cached `--indexed` mode rebuilds stale indexes.

Title: feat(wave): add driver trace, sequences, transactions and wave diff

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

Verdi-style debug capability as CLI and MCP, all generic (no core names):

- `rvw wave why WAVE SIGNAL --at T --db DESIGN.db` (`wave_why`): active-driver tracing. Joins wave values with SpinalDB assignments and their `when`/`switch` chains. Decides the active assignment from condition-signal values (last full-width winner; undecided later candidates give `ambiguous`). Registers are explained at their last value change (`set_at`), with drivers evaluated just before that edge; asserted resets give `status: reset`. Walks back through `data` reads (`--depth`, `--max-nodes`). Output says `binding: unverified` (names joined by wave path).
- `rvw wave seq WAVE 'a ##1 b ##[1:3] c'` (`wave_seq`): clocked sequences with SVA-like delays (`##[n:$]` open), sampled pre-edge; matches, failures (failed step) and pending starts.
- `rvw wave txn` (`wave_txn`): Stream/Flow transfers with payload, wait cycles, stalls, throughput, `payload_changed` and `valid_dropped` issues. `--stream PATH --db DB` types valid/ready/payload from a database bundle.
- `rvw wave diff A B` (`wave_diff`): first divergence between two runs (name pairing, `--map` prefix rename, `--offset`, event or `--on-clock` sampling, `--all`). Status `match`/`diverged`/`no_points`; CLI exit 1 unless `match`.
- Close partly read index merges before the connection closes (removes unraisable sqlite warnings).

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_wave_why.py rvw/tests/test_wave_temporal.py rvw/tests/test_wave_search.py rvw/tests/test_wave.py rvw/tests/test_wave_index.py rvw/tests/test_mcp_tools.py -q`: 194 passed, 0 skipped. `why` uses the committed GCD database with a hand-written GCD wave; `txn --stream` uses the committed cluster database.
- Fast set: 759 passed.
- Not run: real BOOM/Vex waves with their databases, full Python suite.

## Issues

Refs: #297, #24. Adds active-driver tracing, temporal queries, transaction extraction and wave diff with first divergence. Remaining: what-if editing, alignment by retirement/transactions (diff aligns by time only), partial-range bit composition in `why`, real-core parity runs, GUI panels (next PR).

Roadmap notes: debug area — `rvw wave why/seq/txn/diff` (+ MCP) provide driver tracing joined with SpinalDB, SVA-like sequence search, Stream/Flow transaction extraction and first-divergence wave diff.

Title: feat(lint): emit cdc checks from spinal clock-domain data

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- New `SpinalChecks/src/main/scala/spinalchecks/CdcChecks.scala`: `CdcChecks.install(config)` adds an elaboration phase before `PhaseInsertChecks`. It finds every register with Spinal's `crossClockDomain` tag whose data comes, through plain copies, from a register in another clock, and declares:
  - `cdc.gray`: a multi-bit source changes at most one bit per source clock;
  - `cdc.pulse_width`: a one-bit source holds each value for `ceil(settle * f_src / f_dst)` source cycles, when both domains have a Spinal `FixedFrequency`.

Title: feat(debug): add openocd and gdb interoperability campaign

Audit evidence label: reference model only (Spike/Sail/Python).

## Summary
- `rvw debug interop`: GDB starts OpenOCD over a pipe (`gdb_port pipe`) against a remote_bitbang target. The target is a running simulation (`--port`), or the reference model that `rvw debug serve` serves for a profile (`--profile`).
- A GDB Python script checks each operation by its effect: `load` (the entry word equals the ELF bytes), register and memory writes (read back after the caches are flushed), software and hardware breakpoints (stop pc and loop counter), `stepi` and the jump step, a watchpoint (counter advanced, pc after the store), and `monitor reset halt` (pc equals the declared reset pc).
- C3 results (`debug-interop`) record the GDB and OpenOCD versions in `clients`. A connection without these effects is not a pass. A GDB error belongs to the first check it did not reach. Unreached checks are inconclusive.
- Fixture `rvw/tests/fixtures/debug/interop.S`. MCP tool `debug_interop`.

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_debug_dm.py -q`: 36 passed (assessment, C3 attribution, OpenOCD config).

  - Reference model: every check passes.
  - Spike: 7 checks pass. Hardware breakpoint and watchpoint fail. Spike resets each trigger to `tdata1.type` 15, and this OpenOCD skips type-15 triggers ("Couldn't find an available hardware trigger"). The test pins this known outcome.
- Fast set: 808 passed.

Roadmap notes: Debug area. OpenOCD/GDB interoperability is now checked by effect against the reference model and Spike. Finding: OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev cannot use Spike's type-15 reset triggers for hardware breakpoints or watchpoints.

Title: feat(csim): add mockingjay, ipcp, bingo and load address prediction

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- Mockingjay replacement (`replacement: mockingjay`, after Shah, Jain & Lin, HPCA 2022): sampled sets learn a reuse distance per PC signature; lines carry an estimated time remaining that ages with set accesses; scans are trained to the far value and evicted first.
- IPCP data prefetcher (`kind: ipcp`, after Pakalapati & Panda, ISCA 2020): per-IP classes global stream, constant stride, complex stride (signature table) and next line, with per-class counts in the report.
- Bingo data prefetcher (`kind: bingo`, after Bakhshalipour et al., HPCA 2019): SMS-style footprints kept under the long event (PC + address) and the short event (PC + offset); long-event hits are counted.
- Load address prediction section `lap` (last address, stride, context with delta history): coverage, accuracy and misprediction PKI.
- Model catalog, README, contract section list and sweep metrics (`lap_coverage`, `lap_accuracy`) updated. All owner-written from the papers.

Title: feat(debug): check e-trace streams with traps, loss and filters

Audit evidence label: reference model only (Spike/Sail/Python).

## Summary
- E-Trace ingress (`etrace_flow.py`) now covers exceptions, interrupts, trap returns and privilege changes. Trap causes come from C2 trap events. An exception is an exception-only entry at the trapping pc. xRET is reported as itype 6, which is what the pinned baseline encoder and decoder need (see the README).
- `rvw debug etrace-check`: builds the expected stream from C2 with the pinned reference encoder and compares a capture (`.te_inst` or `.te_inst_raw`) field by field. It decodes the capture in segments split at known gaps (`--loss-at`) and trace-lost support packets, resyncs only at sync-start packets, aligns each segment with C2 in order, and reports lost spans as `unknown` windows. It never shows guessed execution. `--filter` (privilege, address ranges, exclusions, start/stop) gives one reference encode per qualified window, and a `leak` verdict for decoded PCs or sync addresses from unqualified execution.
- `rvw debug etrace-loss`: drop, overflow, wrap and truncate faults at sampled positions, with C3 results (`etrace-loss`).
- Test helper `rvw/tests/spike_c2.py` (Spike commit log to C2). Fixture `traps.S` (branches, M-mode and U-mode ecalls, mret).

## Testing
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_debug_trace.py -q`: 11 passed. The tests cover ingress kinds, trap causes, segmentation, injection, windows and verdicts, filters, leaks and packet comparison.
- Native, `RVW_ETRACE_REFERENCE` (pin ffb6bb72) with Spike 1.1.1-dev: `rvw/tests/test_debug_trace_native.py` 4 passed.
  - flow_match and packet_match with exceptions and U-mode.
  - A corrupted branch map gives `mismatch`. A bit for an unobserved branch changes only `packets`.
  - Every loss-campaign fault passes, with unknown windows.
  - An M-only filter gives flow_match for a filtered capture and `leak` for an unfiltered one.
- Fast set: 819 passed.
- Not run: no core RTL encoder capture exists; context changes are not tested.

## Issues
Refs: #168. Open: context changes; options beyond the baseline encoder.
Refs: #172. Open: resync at trap syncs; vendor overflow markers.
Refs: #195. Open: authentication controls; encoder trigger inputs.

Roadmap notes: Trace area. E-Trace checks now cover traps, privilege, loss windows with resynchronization, and qualification filters with leak detection, against the pinned reference flow. Next step: an RTL encoder capture from a core adapter.

Title: feat(debug): add n-trace codec, checks and vendor trace adapters

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary
- `ntrace.py`: a separate, versioned N-Trace codec `rvw-ntrace/1`. It has a reference encoder from C2 (BTM and HTM modes, periodic sync, history and ICNT overflow through ResourceFull, Ownership on privilege change, traps as BTYPE 1), MDO/MSEO byte packing and unpacking, and a decoder that follows the ELF program image. E-Trace support never counts as N-Trace support.
- `rvw debug ntrace-check`: builds the expected stream from C2 (one encode per qualified window when `--filter` is set) and compares captured messages. It decodes in windows split at Error messages, known gaps and decode failures, and resyncs only at ProgTraceSync. Verdicts: `flow_match`, `partial_match`, `mismatch`, `leak`. A capture without its stop message is not a full match.
- `rvw debug ntrace-loss`: drop, overflow (Error), wrap and truncate faults with C3 results (`ntrace-loss`).
- Vendor adapters (`rvw.trace-adapter/1`) and `rvw debug trace-adapter`: an adapter must cite a specification and a license and give known packet vectors that unpack and repack exactly. An adapter without vectors is refused, because a vendor name is not evidence. `examples/trace/nexus-htm-template.toml` is a template whose vectors come from the rvw codec. No SiFive or Andes adapter is bundled, because there are no license-cleared vendor vectors.
- `Asm.auipc` for the model hart.

## Testing
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_debug_ntrace.py -q`: 12 passed. C2 comes from the model hart (branches, M-mode ecall, mret to U-mode, U-mode ecall). The tests cover the round trip, both modes with and without periodic sync, corruption, truncation, filters and leaks, the loss campaign, unmarked loss (mismatch) against marked loss (partial_match), and adapter vectors (pass, missing, wrong).
- Manual: the same flow on the Spike `traps.S` C2 decodes exactly in both modes.
- Fast set: 833 passed.
- Not run: no RTL N-Trace encoder capture; no vendor vectors.

## Issues
Refs: #194. Open: timestamps, multiple SRC, data trace, repeat-branch messages, an RTL encoder capture, and checking the SYNC/EVCODE/ETYPE/RCODE/BTYPE defaults against the ratified N-Trace tables.
Refs: #207. Open: SiFive and Andes adapters need vendor vectors with a usable license.

Roadmap notes: Trace area. N-Trace has its own reference encoder, decoder and loss/filter checks, separate from E-Trace. The vendor adapter mechanism requires packet vectors. Next step: an RTL encoder capture, and vendor vectors.

## Summary

- `rvw csim qualify --reference` gains pinned CBP-5 (2016) references: `cbp2016-mpp-64kb`, `cbp2016-mpp-8kb`, `cbp2016-mpp-unlimited` (D. A. Jiménez, multiperspective perceptron), `cbp2016-mpp-tage-64kb` (MPP with TAGE) and `cbp2016-pruett-64kb`. Archives are fetched into the csim cache and checked by sha256; nothing enters the repository.

Measured on the six Spike benchmark traces: csim hashed perceptron 64 KB vs MPP 64 KB is within about 10% MPKI on all six (qsort 41.75 vs 40.90); csim TAGE-SC-L 64 KB vs MPP unlimited ranges from 0.27 vs 0.36 (dhrystone) to 16.09 vs 12.57 (spmv). Table in `ComponentSims/README.md`.

Title: feat(fault): add fault injection campaigns against c2

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary
- New tool `rvw fault` (`rvw/src/rvw/fault/`, README, Layout row) with these subcommands:
  - `sites`: register sites from the design database (`signals`, kind `reg`, not pruned; generated registers only on request; include/exclude globs).
  - `plan`: a seeded sample of `stuck0`, `stuck1` and `flip` faults over a cycle window. It records the population (site bits × cycles × kinds) and uses exhaustive mode when the population is small.
  - `run`: a golden run plus one run per fault through the core adapter (`run --fault FILE`, new optional C1 extension). The adapter must confirm the injection in `details.fault`, so injection success is measured separately from detection. Each fault is classified against the golden C2 architectural records: `detected` (failure status, a declared mechanism in `details.detections`, or a timeout with `--watchdog`), `silent_corruption`, `safe`, `timeout`, `not_injected` or `inconclusive`.
  - `report`: counts, denominators, sampled fraction, diagnostic coverage with a 95 % Wilson interval, safe fraction, unresolved faults. Outputs also include C3 (`fault-campaign`: detected or safe = pass, SDC = fail) and `outcomes.json` with the evidence for each fault. There is no ISO 26262 or reliability claim.
- MCP: `fault_sites`, `fault_run`, `fault_report`. Contract: "C1 fault injection".

## Testing
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_fault.py -q`: 6 passed. The tests use a fake C1 adapter that runs the debug model hart with a parity checker on one register. Each of detected-by-self-test, detected-by-parity, silent corruption, safe and not-injected (unreached cycle, unknown site) is exercised, together with a refused failing golden run, adapter-confirmation rules, seeded plans and the CLI.
- Fast set: 838 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_release_hygiene.py::test_tracked_text_has_no_personal_paths` on `rvw/tests/cosim/test_adjudicate.py:51`, a file already on main from another area. This change does not touch it.
- Not run: no real core adapter implements `--fault` yet. The RiscvSim BOOM adapter does not.

## Issues
Refs: #52. Done: the stuck-at and transient campaign, injection success measured apart from detection, classification, denominators and coverage. Open: protected-memory codewords, FMEDA records and equivalence groups, lockstep/redundancy campaigns, security fault campaigns, memories as sites, a RiscvSim `--fault` implementation, and tool-qualification documents.

Roadmap notes: Safety area. `rvw fault` gives seeded stuck-at/flip campaigns classified against golden C2, with diagnostic coverage and confidence intervals. Next step: `--fault` in the RiscvSim adapter (Verilator force on database register paths).

Title: feat(csim): add micro-op cache to the front-end model

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- `frontend.op_cache`: a trace-driven micro-op cache in the csim front-end model. Lines are keyed by aligned fetch window (`window_bytes`); a window takes `ceil(ops / ops_per_line)` lines of one set (LRU), more than `max_lines_per_window` is uncacheable. A group hits when all its lines are present: it skips the I-cache and legacy decode and delivers `op_width` ops per cycle after `latency`; each change between op-cache and legacy delivery costs `switch_penalty`. Context rows flush it (default).
- Report: lookups, hit rate, op coverage, fills, uncacheable windows, mode switches, context flushes, storage (`op_bits` per op). Sweep metric `op_cache_coverage`.
- This is the csim component model; the gem5 micro-op cache in #359 stays with the arch area.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest ComponentSims/tests -q` — 99 passed (hit rate and coverage above 95% on a warm loop, higher delivered IPC than legacy decode, tiny cache misses, uncacheable windows, context flush, storage formula).

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests -m fast --strict-markers -q` — 833 passed after rebase.
- Not run: op cracking or fusion (one instruction = one op), full slow suite, CI not awaited.

## Issues

Refs: #360 — front-end component coverage. Refs: #359 (gem5 side, not changed).

Roadmap notes: Component simulators: micro-op cache in the front-end delivery model.

Title: fix(wave): keep fst array names when reading through wellen

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

Fix for the direct FST reader from #529 and the wellen index reader from #412:

- wellen splits Verilator unpacked-array elements into a scope plus an `[i]` variable (`arrays.a.[0]`). Rejoin them as the VCD reader names them (`arrays.a.a[0]`), so searches and indexes use the same names as `fst2vcd`.
- wellen drops the index of escaped Icarus names (`\a[0]` and `\a[1]` become one `\a` variable). Such FSTs now fall back to `fst2vcd` for searches, and an `auto` index build uses the VCD reader. An explicit `--reader wellen` build refuses them (`WellenNames`).
- FSTs that pywellen cannot read also fall back to the converter path, which reports the real error.

## Testing

- `rvw/tests/test_wave_array_names.py` now also runs `search.edges` and `search.find` on real Icarus and Verilator FST/VCD waves. Before the fix, the Verilator FST case returned no matching names and the Icarus FST case merged two elements.
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_wave.py rvw/tests/test_wave_capture.py rvw/tests/test_wave_index.py rvw/tests/test_wave_search.py rvw/tests/test_debug_wave_values.py rvw/tests/test_wave_array_names.py rvw/tests/test_wave_temporal.py -q`: 240 passed, 0 skipped (native Icarus and Verilator from oss-cad-suite).

Title: feat(probes): add simulation probe api and riscvsim event collector

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- New top-level `SpinalProbes/` library: a typed, simulation-only probe API a core designer calls at elaboration: `Probe.branch`, `cacheAccess`, `tlb`, `pageWalk`, `stage`, `retire`, `flush`, `stall`, `csrWrite`, `interruptTaken`, `traceIngress`, `counter` (optional `hpm` selector), `faultSite`, `custom`. Off by default: each call returns at once and adds no hardware unless the elaboration runs under `Probe.enabled(true)`. Enabled calls copy their signals into named public wires `rvwprobe__KIND__NAME__FIELD` in the caller's top scope (also from inside a `when`).
- Why a new library and not inside SpinalKonata: SpinalKonata writes Kanata only and carries a BOOM subproject; probes feed about a dozen consumers and Kanata is one converter among them. The library depends on spinalhdl-core/-sim only.
- RiscvSim: `ProbeCollector` samples enabled probes each cycle into one compact `rvw.probe-events/1` stream (`[cycle, id, values...]`, counters summed into the end record). C1 gets `--probes` (own `ModelKey.probes`, `_probes` model name, replay/identity/build/run-many forwarding, artifact `probe_events`). Adapters opt in with `supportsProbes`; the command line refuses `--probes` otherwise.
- `SpinalProbes/README.md` holds the inventory of every event format the consumer tools expect and which probe feeds each. Contract: new subsection "Probe event stream" in `docs/PLATFORM_CONTRACTS.md`.

## Testing

- `SpinalProbes`: `sbt test` (under the sbt lock): 3 passed (probes off: no `rvwprobe` text in Verilog; on: named wires and sites; name checks).
- `RiscvSim`: `sbt 'testOnly riscvsim.ProbeCollectorSpec'` with Verilator: 2 passed (event rows, counter totals, end record; disabled elaboration has no probes).
- Fast Python set: 847 passed, 2 failed (`test_command_reference.py`, deferred per the brief; this PR adds no CLI command).
- Not run: the full RiscvSim suite, BOOM, any VexRiscv run (next PRs).

## Issues

Refs: #49 (stall-cause and pipeline events now have a producer API; core wiring follows).

Roadmap notes: new component `SpinalProbes/` (generic, simulation-only probe API) with RiscvSim `ProbeCollector` and C1 `--probes`. Status: library and collector done; converters (`rvw probes`), VexRiscv wiring and the bring-your-own-core section follow.

## PR 633

[#633](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/633). Merged: 2026-11-13T03:33:30Z.

Title: feat(query): add a GHDL front end for VHDL designs

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- `rvw query build-hdl --frontend ghdl` elaborates VHDL through the GHDL Yosys plugin (`ghdl --std=08 --work=LIB files -e TOP`). Options: `--library`, `-G NAME=VALUE` (top generics), `--std 93|08` (default 08), `--ghdl-plugin PATH` (else `$RVW_GHDL_PLUGIN`, else the plugin bundled with Yosys). MCP `query_build_hdl` takes `frontend: ghdl` and `library`.
- The plugin writes no source attributes. A second pass, `ghdl --file-to-xml` over the same captured files, gives entity lines (component location), port/signal declaration lines and the first assignment statement line per signal. Component `module` is the entity name (GHDL's `<entity>_B<arch>...` module names are mapped back).
- Clock/reset roots (all `yosys-*` frontends) now follow only ports, aliases, buffers and inverters, and flip edge/polarity per inverter. Before, NEORV32's `rstn_i` was reported active high, because GHDL inverts it for `$adff`. A net derived by other logic is now its own root instead of an arbitrary input found through the logic.
- A register net's `reset_value` is now the concatenation of its own bits' reset values (before, every net got the whole cell's value).
- `scripts/build-ghdl-plugin.py` builds a pinned ghdl-yosys-plugin revision with the GHDL headers of the exact libghdl commit, outside the checkout. The OSS CAD Suite 2026-05-01 plugin emits `$memwr_v2` cells that fail the Yosys cell check, so VHDL memories need the rebuilt plugin.
- Docs: `SpinalDB/README.md` (VHDL section), `docs/contracts/query.md` (GHDL contract section), query README, design note.

## Testing

- `RVW_GHDL_PLUGIN=~/.cache/rvw/lib/ghdl.so RVW_HDL_REF=[local path omitted] rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_query_ghdl.py -q`: 5 passed (synthetic VHDL design with a package record, generics, generate and async reset; independent netlist oracle; refusals; NEORV32 `neorv32_cpu` at 7bd0858). With the bundled plugin: 4 passed, 1 skipped (NEORV32 needs the rebuilt plugin).
- `rvw/tests/test_query_slang.py test_query_hdl.py test_hdl_semantics.py test_lint_hdl.py`: 57 passed.
- `scripts/build-ghdl-plugin.py --cxx clang++` built and loaded the plugin (macOS arm64, about 12 s).
- Fast set (command-reference tests deselected per the brief): 838 passed, 1 skipped.
- Not run: full Python suite, CI, the build script on Linux or with the installer's pinned OSS CAD Suite 2026-10-22 (its plugin revision may need `--plugin-rev`).

## Issues

Refs: #371. Remaining: a second real VHDL design beyond NEORV32 plus the synthetic one, generic values per instance, mixed-language designs, an installer flag for the plugin build, foreign model declarations.

Roadmap notes: Design database front ends: VHDL designs now build through GHDL (`build-hdl --frontend ghdl`) with VHDL declaration and assignment lines; NEORV32 `neorv32_cpu` builds and every `rvw query` command works on it. Clock and reset roots now follow inverters, so reset polarity is that of the input.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Title: feat(query): add a FIRRTL and CIRCT front end for Chisel

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- `rvw query build-hdl --frontend chisel` takes one FIRRTL file (`ChiselStage.emitCHIRRTL`). firtool (`--firtool`, `$RVW_FIRTOOL`, `PATH`) writes split Verilog and HGLDD (`-g --emit-hgldd --disable-all-randomization`, plain location comments). The native reader imports the Verilog with `-DSYNTHESIS`; `opt_dff` folds Chisel's synchronous resets into `$sdff`, so registers get `SYNC` domains and reset values.
- Scala origin and emitted RTL are separate bindings: database locations are rebound from firtool's `// Gen.scala:13:20` comments to Scala files captured under `--source-root` (declarations take the first location of a line, assignments the last). No location points at emitted Verilog. The Verilog stays as artifacts `rtl/*.sv`, with `hdl/source-map.json` (Verilog line -> Scala locations) and firtool's `hgldd/*.dd` (`rvw query export hgldd/Top.dd` for SpinalWaves/Surfer).
- HGLDD names become each signal's second spelling: `rvw query where io.a.valid` finds `io_a_valid`.
- Unresolved extern modules are refused by `hierarchy -check`. firtool errors keep an old database.
- Test oracles (`test_query_hdl._yosys_graph`, `test_query_slang._oracle`) now link memory write ports to read ports; before, they missed every path through a memory.
- MCP `query_build_hdl`: `frontend: chisel`, `source_roots`. Docs: `SpinalDB/README.md`, `docs/contracts/query.md`, query README, design note.

## Testing

- `RVW_FIRTOOL=<Chisel's cached firtool 1.62.0> rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_query_chisel.py rvw/tests/test_query_hdl.py rvw/tests/test_query_slang.py rvw/tests/test_query_ghdl.py -q`: 25 passed, 1 skipped (NEORV32 needs `RVW_GHDL_PLUGIN`). The Chisel fixture (`rvw/tests/data/chisel/Gen.scala`, `Top.fir`) was emitted by Chisel 6.5.0: two `Acc` instances, a `Mem`, a `Valid` bundle and a `Vec` port. Paths are compared with an independent Yosys traversal of the emitted Verilog.
- Fast set (command-reference tests deselected per the brief): 852 passed, 1 skipped.

Roadmap notes: Design database front ends: Chisel designs now build from FIRRTL through firtool (`build-hdl --frontend chisel`); locations point at Scala lines, Chisel names resolve, and the emitted Verilog and HGLDD are stored in the database.

Title: feat(sim): bridge verilator systemc rtl to tlm memory

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

Add a generic blocking TLM-2 memory target with byte enables, range checks, annotated delay and explicit refusal of unsupported streaming bursts. Add a tiny RTL requester built with Verilator --sc and a SystemC initiator bridge. The requester writes a word, reads it back and checks the value in RTL.

Define timing and ordering: one initiator, one outstanding transfer, falling-edge request sampling, 2 ns annotated latency consumed before response, 10 ns clock. - The first dependency discovery skipped because the Homebrew SystemC package has no pkg-config file. The test supports explicit SYSTEMC_HOME; the native rerun passed with that prefix.
- Fast set before final fetch/rebase: 878 passed, 1 skipped, 7320 deselected. Command-reference check deferred by the work brief.
- CLI import passed after rebase.
- NOT RUN: full Python suite, BOOM, multi-initiator operation, temporal decoupling, interrupts, whole-core SystemC, checkpoint restore and GitHub CI.

Title: feat(query): write SpinalBlocks diagrams for HDL databases

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- New `rvw/src/rvw/query/blocks.py` derives a SpinalBlocks diagram (format version 1) from any design database's tables. One diagram per module name (first instance in path order, `instanceCount` over all), ports (record fields grouped), instances, one node per named register (`sig:`) or memory (`mem:`), and nets traced backwards through wires, bit nodes and hidden cell hubs to driver endpoints. Register bits stand for their register; a registered output port gets its own node only when no internal register holds its bits; `control` and `clock` flags from edge kinds and clock roles.

Title: feat(riscvsim): inject faults through verilator public access

Audit evidence label: ran on seeded RTL fixture.

## Summary
- Generic `run --fault FILE` (C1 fault injection) in `RiscvSim/src` for any adapter that runs through `SimSession`; no adapter code and no core names.
- Fault jobs use a separate `_fault` model: an elaboration phase tags every register `simPublic`, and Verilator gets `--public-flat-rw` so outside writes re-evaluate readers. Golden runs keep the normal model.
- The injector resolves `site` as the design-database register path, writes the bit after each clock edge in the window (`stuck0`/`stuck1` for `duration` or to the end, `flip` once), and confirms by reading the register back one time unit later. `details.fault` adds `applied_cycle`, `before`, `after`, `writes`. Missing sites, enumeration registers, out-of-range bits, runs that end first and failed read-backs give `applied: false` with a reason. Replay commands carry `--fault`.
- Docs: `docs/contracts/c2-rvfi-trace.md` ("RiscvSim harness hooks"), `RiscvSim/README.md` ("Fault injection"), fault README.

## Testing
- Native, VexRiscv example (`VEXRISCV` = shared checkout at `a62c145a`, under the `vex` lock): `examples/vexriscv/rvw/tests/test_fault_native.py`: 1 passed (flip of `CsrPlugin_mscratch` bit 4 confirmed by read-back; a missing site gives `not_injected`).
- Real campaign with `rvw fault` on VexRiscv (smoke, 91 cycles): plan of 12 faults from the design database (`--exclude '*FORMAL*'`, window 10:80, seed 7). 11 applied and confirmed; 2 detected (asserts), 4 timeouts, 5 safe, 1 `not_injected` (`CsrPlugin_satp_PPN`, absent from the current M-only model; the database came from an older config). Diagnostic coverage 0.33 (95 % 0.10..0.70) over 6 unsafe outcomes.
- `sbt root/compile` of the VexRiscv example (RiscvSim via ProjectRef) under the sbt lock: success.
- Fast set: 900 passed, 1 skipped.
- Not run: BOOM (its adapter uses `SimSession`, so it gets the hook, but it is untested); RiscvSim's own sbt tests (they load BOOM).

## Issues
Refs: #52 (adapter-side injection now exists; FMEDA, memories as sites and lockstep checks remain).

Roadmap notes: functional safety: `rvw fault run` now runs against core RTL through the generic RiscvSim `--fault` hook; first real VexRiscv campaign measured.

Title: fix(cosim): sample vexriscv events before dpi synchronization

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
Sample the VexRiscv trap, RVFI record and CSR snapshot before any DPI call can yield simulation time. This fixes a real missed retirement at interrupt entry without weakening the strict order check.

Add native MSIP and MTIP lockstep tests. The positive controls initialize mtval to zero, assert the input at cycle 200, deassert it at cycle 220, check the real trap cause, execute the handler and MRET, and require a complete Spike match.

Keep negative controls for the pinned core's retained mtval behavior. With mtval initialized to 7, both interrupts must mismatch at the trap boundary: Spike expects zero, RTL reports 7. No mask, fabricated trap value or core-source change is used. General interrupt correctness is not claimed.

## Testing
Native counts are recorded in the example README. Fast-set results are recorded below before publication.
NOT RUN: BOOM, full Python suite, other VexRiscv configurations, general interrupt compliance.

## Issues
The pinned VexRiscv CSR implementation writes mtval only on an exception; interrupt entry retains its previous value. This core/reference difference remains open. The native negative controls preserve it as a visible mismatch.

Roadmap notes: Native VexRiscv MSIP/MTIP lockstep synchronization is exercised through handler entry and MRET with explicit mtval preconditions. A retained-mtval mismatch remains; it is not waived.

Validation: native controls 4 passed. The two zero-mtval runs each matched 50 instructions and one interrupt trap, including the cycle-220 input deassertion. The two nonzero-mtval runs each detected the real tval mismatch. Fast set: 934 passed, 1 skipped, 7399 deselected.

- **Bug fix found by the probes:** `rvw csim` C2 and Spike converters wrote the fall-through as the target of a not-taken conditional branch. - `branches --probes --rvfi-trace`: pass, 35659 instructions, 195928 cycles. `probe-events.jsonl` complete; 9002 branch events (6001 cond).
- `rvw probes convert --to bp-events` + `rvw csim compare-rtl`:
  - `btfn.json`: before the fix 1 disagreement (loop exit at `0x8000006c`); after the fix 0 of 6001, 3355 misses each (94.1 MPKI).
  - `gshare.json` (1024 entries, 10 bits): agreement 44.3 %, 1199 model misses (33.6 MPKI).
- `--to kanata` + `rvw perf`: IPC 0.182, exact cycle/instret match with `result.json`; 160269 inferred `fetch/empty` cycles.
- `irqs --irq-schedule '1:0x0,2000:0x80,2200:0x0,4000:0x800,4200:0x0,6000:0x80,6200:0x0'`: pass; `--to interrupts` consistent (3 probe events, 3 C2 interrupts); `--to counts` and `--to hpm` (3 bindings) written. Re-run after the rebase onto main with the same result.
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_csim_formats.py -q`: 17 passed (2 new tests; the not-taken target test fails before the fix).
- Fast set: 880 passed, 1 skipped.

Not run: the VexRiscv example pytest suite, sbt test suites, the full Python suite, CI.

## Issues

Refs: probes follow-up (VexRiscv wiring, item 1 of 6).

Roadmap notes: SpinalProbes now has a second user (VexRiscv example) with real BTFN/gshare, Kanata, interrupt, counts and HPM conversions. Component sims: the C2/Spike converters keep decoded targets on not-taken branches.

Title: feat(probes): add bus and csr-write probes with c2 consistency checks

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

- SpinalProbes: new `Probe.bus(bus, valid, address, write, data, mask, size)` kind `bus` (one accepted request at a core port, before any cache). Contract text in `docs/contracts/sim.md`.
- VexRiscv `ProbePlugin`: `bus ibus` / `bus dbus` on accepted `iBus`/`dBus` commands; `csrWrite csr` from `csrMapping.onAnyWrite` (the CSR plugin's own `writeEnable`), the instruction's CSR field and `writeDataSignal`. New `memcsr.S` program (word/half/byte loads and stores, all six CSR forms, one illegal `csrw satp`).
- `rvw probes convert --to bus` (`rvw.probe-bus-check/1`): data bus writes against retired C2 stores one to one (bytes and values, in order); each retired C2 load covered by a later bus read in order; `unretired_reads` counts speculative reads.
- `rvw probes convert --to csr-writes` (`rvw.probe-csr-writes/1`): each retired C2 CSR write matches the next write event by address, and by value when C2 operands give it. An extra event is accepted only for an access that trapped (trapped C2 record, or a C2 exception before the next retirement whose illegal-instruction `tval` names the same CSR).
- New consumer rows `bus-check` and `csr-write-check` in `rvw probes list`. Code in a new module `rvw/src/rvw/probes/checks.py`.

## Testing

Native, private VexRiscv copy (core sources `baf7dc82`), lock `vex-csims`, seed 1:

- `memcsr --probes --rvfi-trace`: pass, 382 instructions, 1855 cycles. Re-run after the rebase: same result.
- `--to bus`: consistent. 61 bus writes = 61 C2 stores (bytes and values), 60 reads cover 60 loads, 0 unretired reads.
- `--to csr-writes`: first run found a mismatch: the core strobes the write port for the illegal `csrw satp` (C2 records only a trap event, cause 2). After the trap rule: consistent, 123 events, 122 retired writes, 122 values checked, 1 trapped strobe.
- `--to hpm`: loads 60, stores 61, mispredicts 1.
- Per-slot CSR capture: `rvw cosim check` against Spike (shim rebuilt with `Cosim/build.sh`): `match`, 382 instructions, `csr_snapshot` `0x340` on all 382 steps.
- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_probes_checks.py rvw/tests/test_probes.py -q`: 18 passed (8 new). The trapped-strobe test fails before the fix.
- Fast set: 1297 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed: `rvw/tests/test_docs_site.py::test_docs_staging_does_not_write_sources` (README staging; not in files this PR touches).

Not run: cache probes. This VexRiscv config has no caches (`IBusSimplePlugin`, `DBusSimplePlugin`), and VexiiRiscv on main is cacheless too. A cached config would change the bus type that the other VexRiscv example tools drive, so the cache observer check stays without input. Not run either: sbt test suites, the VexRiscv example pytest suite, the full Python suite, CI.

## Issues

Refs: probes follow-up (item 2 of 6: CSR writes and bus transactions done; cache access/miss not possible on the cacheless configs).

Roadmap notes: SpinalProbes has a `bus` kind; `rvw probes` checks bus and CSR-write probes against C2 on VexRiscv (both consistent). Cache probes still need a cached core config.

Title: fix(query): stop packed HDL aliases from connecting unrelated lanes

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary
Fix cross-lane paths introduced by packed HDL aliases. A multi-bit HDL signal is an endpoint view of the bit nodes. Query traversal can start or end there, but must not traverse through that view to connect different lanes. Keep memory and synchronous read-state nodes as actual boundaries. This also handles generated packed aliases.

The new fast tests construct two independent scalar lanes with a packed alias and check paths, fanin and fanout. They retain real connections and aggregate endpoint queries while rejecting cross-lane paths.

## Testing

The profile found 525,969 port reads and 401,655 writes against 120,497 evaluations. The follow-up measured 1.222x CPU throughput with snapshots and exact complete C2 equality. Wall throughput in that sample was lower, ratio 0.862, so no snapshot wall-time gain is claimed. Preserve the earlier noisy campaign too.

The 49-test ISA suite took 16.84 seconds in one server and 422.41 seconds in separate JVMs. All tests passed and all complete C2 files matched. This is a measured 25.08x JVM-reuse throughput ratio, not an isolated RTL kernel speedup.

- Persistent ISA comparison: 49 conclusive passes per mode, 49 complete C2 matches, 17,735 retirements. One warm native-cache run preceded measurement. Whole-suite throughput: 41.99 -> 1,053.09 instructions/s. Scala compilation and common tool/source capture excluded.

Title: feat(debug): serve rtl debug modules over dmi and jtag from project data

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
- Generic RiscvSim debug endpoints (`RiscvSim/src`, no core names), bound from `rvw.debug-binding/1`:
  - `--debug dmi`: the C1 DMI line protocol on stdin/stdout (cmd/rsp ports from the binding, busy and fail, `t` ticks).
  - `--debug jtag:PORT`: remote_bitbang pin driver for TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO (+ optional TRST). One client at a time; `Q` or EOF ends a client; the session ends after `idle_timeout_s` without a client. Title: feat(sec): run security techniques natively on the example cores

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Run the `rvw sec` techniques on the two example cores, in native Verilator runs of RTL generated from the pinned example revisions.

- `rvw/src/rvw/sec/rtl.py`: generic harness for a core's exported Verilog, bound by project data (`rvw.sec-core/1`): RAM with a per-word taint shadow, in-order bus responses, RVFI or commit-port C2 capture (trapped instructions synthesized from trap events), cycle-stamped bus and retirement observations.
- `python -m rvw.sec.core_adapter`: a ready `adapter_command` for `sec contract` / `sec isolation`. It renders the case (fixed-length secret setup), builds the ELF, makes the Spike reference with `rvw cosim generate`, and runs the RTL.
- `rvw sec ift-core` (MCP `sec_ift_core`): whole-core Boolean taint on the Yosys gate netlist. Secrets are ELF memory regions (per-word RAM taint) or register netnames (CSR). Sinks are bus address and handshake outputs.
- `rvw sec spec-suite` (MCP `sec_spec_suite`): RV32 v1, v2, rsb, v4 gadgets under `speculative-constant-time`, with bus-trace and timing receivers.
- Paired runner: `{python}` in adapter argv, `observations`/`contract_start_pc`/`observer_mode` in the request, adapter-declared `c2_keys`, failed reduction trials recorded as `rejected_trials`.
- Example project data: `examples/vexriscv/rvw/sec/` (bindings for `rv32im`, user-mode `rv32imu`, and a deliberately leaky patched copy), `examples/vexiiriscv/rvw/sec/`, and `SecRtl` Verilog generators.

Real results (full table in `rvw/src/rvw/sec/README.md`):

- VexiiRiscv constant-time: **violation**, reduced to `remu x13, x6, x7` (14 against 38 cycles). Its `DivRadix2` divider latency depends on operands. VexRiscv: every divide takes 34 cycles, `no_leak_observed`.
- IFT: constant-time XOR is clean on both cores. A secret branch taints the fetch address; a secret table index taints the data bus address; a CSR (`mscratch`) source works on VexRiscv.
- Isolation M/U on VexRiscv `rv32imu`: constant-time handler `no_leak_observed`; secret-dependent handler (control) violation, 48 against 84 cycles per system call.
- Speculative suite (VexRiscv): the unpatched core shows none for all four gadgets; the patched copy (flushed loads issue) shows v1, v2 and rsb violations in the bus trace.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_sec*.py -q`: pass.
- Fast set: 1575 passed, 2 failed in files I did not touch: `test_mcp_coherence.py::test_discovery_audit_baseline` (`formal_sva_inspect` has no side_effects/native_tools) and `test_release_hygiene.py::test_tracked_text_has_no_personal_paths` (`docs/status/2026-11-13/PR_EVIDENCE.md`).

Title: feat(probes): convert walk results and fault sites, feed ooo calibration

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Converters for the consumers in the event inventory that still had none:

- **Page walks → C2 `mmu_walks`.** New `Probe.walkResult(walker, mode, valid, va, access, root, status, pa)` (kind `walk`, meta `event=result`). `rvw probes convert --to mmu-walks --c2 TRACE` groups each walker's `response` events up to its result into one `mmu_walk` record (sequential `access_id`, validated with `rvw.regress.mmu_walk.validate_capture`). It attaches each record to the first retirement at or after the result cycle, in a new copy of the trace. `rvw regress mmu report`'s walk checker then reads it. Walks after the last retirement are reported as `unattached`. `--to mmu` skips result events.
- **Fault sites.** `ProbeCollector` writes `meta.path` for `fault` probes (the path that C1 `--fault` resolves). `--to fault-sites` writes a site list. `rvw fault sites|plan --sites FILE` takes it in place of `--db`. The VexRiscv plugin declares `mscratch` as a site.
- **OoO calibration counters.** `--to counts` already wrote the `rvw arch ooo-calibrate` RTL event file. The real run showed that the OoO model refused every VexRiscv trace (the C2 levels-0 `irq` event). Main fixed that in parallel. I kept main's fix and added `test_ooo_zero_irq.py`. A VexRiscv in-order model config and an event map are in `examples/vexriscv/rvw/probes/ooo/`.
- Consumer rows `mmu-walk-records` and `fault-sites` are now enabled. Contracts in `docs/contracts/sim.md`. Notes in the SpinalProbes, probes, fault and VexRiscv READMEs.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_probes_records.py rvw/tests/test_probes.py rvw/tests/test_probes_checks.py rvw/tests/test_ooo_zero_irq.py rvw/tests/test_ooo.py rvw/tests/test_fault.py -q`: 53 passed. New: a walk round trip through `check_c2` (consistent), wrong PTE data (mismatch), unattached walks, unknown codes, fault-site plan and the `--sites` CLI.
- Native VexRiscv (private copy, lock `vex-csims`):
  - `memcsr --probes`: `--to fault-sites` gives `CsrPlugin_mscratch` (32 bits).
  - `rvw fault plan --sites` (flip/stuck1, window 100:1700, 4 samples, seed 7) and `rvw fault run`: 4 of 4 injected, 4 `silent_corruption`.
  - `branches` and `smoke --probes` → `--to counts` → `rvw arch ooo-calibrate`: reported. `retired` and `branches` match the model exactly. Mispredicts: model 7854 against core 4855. IPC error 224.5 % (training) and 105.2 % (held out). Accuracy `inconclusive`.
- Fast set: 1458 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed: `rvw/tests/test_docs_site.py::test_docs_staging_does_not_write_sources` (not in files this PR touches).

Not run: no core on main has an MMU, so `mmu-walks` is tested on synthetic streams only (the second-core item adds a Verilator run). Also not run: sbt test suites, the full Python suite, CI.

Title: feat(debug): check rtl trace ingress against c2 with e-trace and n-trace

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
- RiscvSim `run --trace-ingress FILE` (generic, `RiscvSim/src`): samples a project-declared E-Trace encoder ingress port (`rvw.trace-ingress-binding/1`: sources with a `valid` port and column → port or constant) into `te_ingress.csv` (artifact `trace_ingress`, reference-encoder columns). `details.trace_ingress` records rows.
- `rvw debug ingress-check` (CLI + MCP `debug_ingress_check`, `rvw.trace-ingress-check/1`): (1) every RTL row against the row derived from C2; (2) N-Trace: rebuild the flow from ingress + ELF, encode with the rvw codec, decode with the ELF, compare PCs with C2; (3) E-Trace with `--reference`: pinned reference encoder + decoder on the RTL ingress. `match` only when every part matches; mismatch exit 1; otherwise inconclusive.
- `etrace_flow.retirement(path, code=...)`: a C2 trap event with no retirement row for the trapping instruction (VexRiscv C2) is rebuilt at the previous `pc_next` when the ELF is given; without it the trace is still refused.
- VexRiscv example (additive): `rv32im_trace` config with `TraceIngressPlugin` (write-back retirement rows; trap rows from actual mcause/mtval/mepc storage) and `trace/ingress-binding.json`.
- Docs: contract bullet in `docs/contracts/c2-rvfi-trace.md`, debug README "Trace ingress from a core", example README.

Title: feat(probes): validate event streams and name misplaced probes

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

`rvw probes check` (added in #895 for presence only) now validates an event stream against the `rvw.probe-events/1` contract and names the misplaced probe:

- `--validate` checks:
  - the stream reads under the contract;
  - each value fits its field width;
  - end record: its cycle is not before the last event, and its per-probe counts equal the rows;
  - each counter has a total, and the total fits its active cycles (a 1-bit counter equals them) and the cycle count;
  - retire and flush IDs were staged, close once, and are not staged again (ID reuse or an early retire);
  - each walker's responses end in a result, and a successful result has responses.
- `--c2 TRACE` (implies `--validate`) runs the branch (`bp-events` alignment), interrupt, data bus and CSR-write checks, and compares retire events with C2 retirements.
- Each finding has `probe` (`kind/name`), `check`, `severity`, `message` and `first_cycle`. Status `violations` gives exit 1; a missing end record gives `inconclusive` (exit 3). `clean` is not a wiring proof.
- MCP `probes_check` takes `validate` and `c2`. Contract text: `docs/contracts/probes.md` ("Stream validation"). Code: new module `rvw/src/rvw/probes/validate.py`.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_probes_validate.py rvw/tests/test_probes_check.py rvw/tests/test_probes.py rvw/tests/test_probes_checks.py rvw/tests/test_probes_records.py -q`: 37 passed. 11 new tests: unstaged retire, stage after retire, width, end counts, counter totals, incomplete stream, bad format, walk grouping, a speculative branch probe against C2, retire count against C2, CLI exit codes, MCP schema.

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary

Synthesis safety for SpinalProbes: disabled probes must not change the generated Verilog.

- `SpinalProbes/src/test/scala/spinalprobes/ProbeSafetySpec.scala`: a seeded three-stage pipeline (register file, TLB tag, cache tag, branch unit, CSR register). Its `withProbes` variant calls every probe kind (branch, cache, tlb, pageWalk, walkResult, stage, retire, flush, stall, csrWrite, interruptTaken, traceIngress, bus, counter, faultSite, custom). With probes disabled, its Verilog must be byte-identical to the variant without calls. With probes enabled, the Verilog must contain every kind's wires, so the test can fail.
- Real cores: `rvwvex.ProbeSafety` (VexRiscv with and without `ProbePlugin`) and `rvwvexii.ProbeSafety` (VexiiRiscv `rv32im` and `rv32imasu`, with and without `ProbeTapPlugin`). Each prints both SHA-256 values and exits 1 on a difference. `VexTop.configuration(probePlugin = true)` selects the plugin.

## Testing

- `cd SpinalProbes && ../scripts/with-lock.sh sbt nice -n 10 sbt -batch -Dsbt.offline=true test`: 5 tests passed, 0 failed (2 new).
- `rvwvex.ProbeSafety` (private VexRiscv copy, `baf7dc82`): identical, `1ba7bb07c57505a6…` both.
- `rvwvexii.ProbeSafety` (private VexiiRiscv copy, `9f70315d`): `rv32im` identical (`af58b6d9c4f6c3e3…`), `rv32imasu` identical (`eee00998072f0dbe…`).
- No Python change; the last fast set (this session) was 1650 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed outside the probe area (`test_docs_site.py::test_docs_staging_does_not_write_sources`, `test_release_hygiene.py::test_tracked_text_has_no_personal_paths`).

Title: feat(sec): add resumable coverage-guided leakage campaigns

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

The campaign loop for paired leakage testing: `rvw sec campaign --manifest M --out D [--resume]` (MCP `sec_campaign`).

- Grammar-based RV32IM program generation (alu, alui, mul, div, load, store, branch). Secrets stay out of addresses and branch conditions.
- Input mutation: program insert/delete/replace (a branch stays with its label) and secret-pair mutation (bit flips, boundary values).
- Coverage feedback from microarchitectural observations: per-instruction retirement latency, bus trace lengths, probe branch outcomes and probe counter values. Pairs with new keys join the corpus.
- Contract selection (round robin over `contracts`), violation minimisation with the paired reducer, deduplication by root-cause signature (reduced mnemonics and differing channels).
- Budgets in pairs and seconds; `state.json` after each pair; `--resume` continues; C3 `results.json`, `report.json` and `report.md`.
- Fix found by the first campaign: VexRiscv RVFI replicates byte-store data across the word, so 13 of 24 pairs were inconclusive. Store data now compares on its written byte lanes, as `rvw cosim` does.

Results (24 pairs per core, both contracts):

| Core | Outcomes | Signatures |
|---|---|---|
| VexiiRiscv | 18 no_leak_observed, 6 violations | `remu` (`remu x15, x7, x5`), `div` (`div x10, x7, x10`) |
| VexRiscv | 24 no_leak_observed | none |

This branch also carries two small harness hooks used by the next PRs (`soc` path in the core binding, the tainted-RAM dump in IFT runs, `rtl_required=False` for model-only use).

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_sec_suite.py rvw/tests/test_sec_core.py rvw/tests/test_sec_campaign.py -q`: 17 passed. The campaign tests use a fake adapter whose divide latency depends on the secret.

Title: feat(sec): predict contract-pair leakage on the ooo timing model

Audit evidence label: reference model only (Spike/Sail/Python).

## Summary

A model-level leakage pre-check: `rvw sec model-check --manifest M --out D` (MCP `sec_model_check`). It runs the same contract pairs on the trace-driven OoO timing model (`rvw/src/rvw/ooo/`) to predict leakage of a planned microarchitecture before RTL exists.

- Each secret's program runs on Spike. Its C2 trace drives the model description (`rvw.arch-core/1` or an `ooo` table).
- `operand_latency` states planned unit behavior per class: `fixed`, `quotient_bits` (divider that skips zero quotient bits) or `early_out` (narrow-operand multiplier). Rules read operands from the reference trace and become per-instruction custom latency classes.
- Equal architectural contract traces with different predicted cycles are a predicted violation. Reports say the evidence is a model prediction, not RTL evidence.

Results (examples' in-order model descriptions):

| Manifest | Rule | Predicted cycles | Prediction | RTL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vexiiriscv model-precheck | divide quotient_bits | 28 vs 57 | violation | violation (remu 14 vs 38) |
| vexriscv model-precheck | divide fixed 34 | 56 vs 56 | no_leak_observed | no_leak_observed |
| vexiiriscv model-precheck-mul | multiply early_out | 25 vs 33 | violation | planned unit, no RTL |

The model predicts the direction of both RTL results, not the cycle counts.

## Testing

- `rvw/.venv/bin/python -m pytest rvw/tests/test_sec_model_check.py rvw/tests/test_sec_suite.py -q`: 7 passed (rule arithmetic; synthetic C2 trace on the model with dependent, fixed and no rules).
- Native: the three manifests above with Spike and the RISC-V GCC.
- MCP audit: no new debt for `sec_*` tools.
- Not run: the full fast set (only `rvw/src/rvw/sec` changed), transient or cache predictions (the model is committed-path only).

## Issues

Refs: none.

Roadmap notes: `rvw sec model-check` predicts timing leakage of a planned unit on the OoO model before RTL; it agrees in direction with both example cores' RTL results.

- Isolation pair: `no_leak_observed`. The RTL takes a load access fault (cause 0xd, tval 0x80008000) exactly as Spike does. The denied load is absent from the data bus trace; the dependent load uses the public address for both secrets (30 cycles each).
- IFT: `no_leak_observed`; no tainted data left the keystore.

Title: feat(probes): add cached vexriscv and vexiiriscv example configs

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Cached configurations for both example cores, without changes to the core sources. `rv32im` stays the default in both projects.

- VexRiscv `rv32im_cached`: `IBusCachedPlugin` + `DBusCachedPlugin` with the `GenFullNoMmu` caches (4 KiB, 32-byte lines, 1 way, write-through D$ with no allocation on a store miss).
- VexRiscv `rv32ima_linux`: the same caches with LR/SC and AMOs, `MmuPlugin` (Sv32, 4-entry port TLBs), M/S/U CSRs. `rvw/platform-linux.json` is its Spike platform.
- VexiiRiscv `rv32im_cached`: upstream fetch L1 and LSU L1 (64-byte lines, 2 ways x 32 sets, write-back LSU L1) and the upstream BTB + RAS + GShare.
- `CachedFormalPlugin` (VexRiscv): `DBusCachedPlugin` does not feed the RVFI memory fields; they are rebuilt at write-back (masks, store data, load word lanes, AMO result, SC success).
- `CachedBuses` (VexRiscv) and `L1Buses` (VexiiRiscv) answer the cache buses (line refills one word per cycle after the run's latency; Vexii writeback bursts).
- VexiiRiscv `SpinalConfig(inlineRom = true)`: the predictor RAMs have simulation init content, and RiscvSim's RTL identity needs one generated file. Configs without such RAMs give the same Verilog.
- New suites `isa-cached` (both) and `isa-linux` (VexRiscv). `build-tests.sh` (VexRiscv) also builds `rv32ua-p`.

Title: fix(privilege): read regress outputs once and refuse unearned fails

Audit evidence label: unit tests only.

## Summary
Two defects found when the third dry-run pass ran the generated RV32 interrupt suites on the independent core and checked them with `rvw privilege check`.

1. **Duplicate C1 results.** `privilege check`, `regress/mmu.py` (two checks) and `regress/vector.py` used `Path(results).rglob('result.json')`. A `rvw regress run --out` directory holds each run twice (sealed generation and current view), so every scenario had two candidates and stayed "need one conclusive C1 result" forever. A new `run_evidence.run_paths_under` stops at each owned root and reads its members once through the existing `owned_run_paths`. A parent of several regression outputs still works.
2. **Unearned fails.** The strict comparison failed a correct core when it read `mip` with a pending external interrupt pin, or loaded `mtime` from a declared MMIO CLINT. Spike models neither. Only these exact shapes are now `inconclusive` with a reason: a CSR read of mip whose differing bits are all platform `irq_inputs`, and a load in a platform `mmio` region that differs only in the loaded value. All other mismatches still fail. Nothing new can pass.

Roadmap notes: on the dry-run RV32 core, the RV32 `wfi-clint` and `scheduled-wfi` suites now give 4 strict passes and 6 explicit inconclusives (external pins / device reads), and all 10 match Spike with irq/mmio synchronization.

## Testing
- `pytest rvw/tests/test_privilege_campaign.py test_regress_run_evidence.py`: all passed. The new tests cover irq bits, non-irq bits, a non-mip CSR, extra difference fields, MMIO/RAM loads, and a store/parent tree with duplicate members.
- `pytest rvw/tests -m fast -k "mmu or vector or privilege or run_evidence"`: 143 passed.
- Native: `rvw privilege check` on the dry-run regression output (10 RTL runs) before and after.

VexRiscv gets `rvw/features.json`, `rvw/prepare-suites.py` and `rvw-suites.toml`.
- **Adapter fixes (VexiiRiscv).** The previous worker's VA capture read a 64-bit signal with `toLong` (every RV64 program asserted). An AMO's store half has a stale probe store id; it now binds to the latest hart command at its physical address. C2 `tval` now uses the core's own CSR write expression (`expendPc`), which fixes the `sv39-noncanonical-negative` mismatch. The VA tap is optional so `rv32im_cached` still elaborates. 16/9 ASID bits (previous commit).
- **Page-walk observation path.** `WalkTap` reads the MMU refill state machine (start request, PTE reads on the walker port, refill response with the walker's permission check). `WalkCapture` turns that into C2 `mmu_walks`. RiscvSim `RvfiRecord.extra` appends adapter-observed fields. `rvw regress mmu report` then compares against the independent walker. `mmu_walk.same_run` now accepts the runner fields that `rvw regress run` adds to C1 `source`; before, every walk check under a regress run was inconclusive.
- **`rvw regress cosim RUN --platform P [--allow-sync reset,irq]`** (MCP `regress_cosim`): one status per C1 result (`match`, `mismatch`, `fail`, `error`, `inconclusive`), counts per suite. Strict by default; `reset` allows only the unspecified `mscratch` reset value, `irq` only pending bits of asserted inputs. Contract in `docs/contracts/vexii.md`.
- **Numbers** in the VexiiRiscv, VexRiscv, MMU, privilege and ordering READMEs and in `docs/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`.

Title: fix(cosim): compare split ram accesses under uniform pmp and u-mode

Audit evidence label: reference model only (Spike/Sail/Python).

## Summary
The third dry-run pass added U-mode and four PMP entries to the independent RV32 core. The riscv-tests `p` environment then runs the tests in U-mode under its all-memory NAPOT entry, and the `scalar_split_ram` comparison (from #954) refused `rv32ui-p-ma_data` again: it required M-mode and zero PMP regions.

The shim now accepts a split RAM access when:
- the effective mode (after MPRV) is M, or U on a core without S-mode (no translation);
- `mseccfg` is zero;
- PMP decides every byte the same way, by Spike's rule: the lowest entry that matches any byte matches all bytes and `access_ok` allows the access, or no entry matches and the mode is M.

Partial matches, denied accesses, page splits, MMIO overlap and partial faults stay refused. No ABI change. The contract and `Cosim/README.md` text are updated.

Roadmap notes: on the dry-run core with U-mode and PMP, all 61 RTL traces (42 rv32ui-p, 8 rv32um-p, smoke, 10 RV32 interrupt programs) match Spike.

- `pytest rvw/tests/cosim/test_scalar_split_ram.py rvw/tests/test_scalar_split_policy.py`: 14 passed (native Spike shim). New: unlocked PMP and a locked RWX entry give a match; a locked R/X-only entry refuses the split store. The new match cases failed before the fix.
- Native: `rv32ui-p-ma_data` on the dry-run U-mode core: refused before, `match` (419 instructions) after.

Title: feat(vexii): run clint wfi suites through isolated device plugins

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Run the CLINT-driven WFI family on VexiiRiscv RTL through the DeviceApiV1 CPython plugin.

- **Isolated device library.** `RiscvSim/scripts/build-devices.py` compiles the interpreter home and this workstation's `rvw/src` into `PythonDevices.cpp`, which then starts an isolated interpreter (`PyConfig_InitIsolatedConfig`). Before, the profile needed `PYTHONHOME`/`PYTHONPATH`, and native identity refuses both ("cannot enumerate ... inputs"), so every regress run of `rvw64-devices.toml` was `input_not_captured`. A library built without the defines still reads the environment. `run64-devices.sh` now refuses the two variables.
- **MMIO store fix.** The adapter passed the whole 64-bit bus data for a narrow MMIO store; the bus replicates a word in both lanes, so a 4-byte MSIP write exceeded 32 bits and the model refused it (C1 assert). It now masks the value to the access width.
- **Selection and suites.** `rvw/features64-devices.json` adds `device:clint`; `prepare-suites.py` builds the `wfi-clint` family when `rvw regress plan` selects it. `rvw64-devices.toml` runs the four programs.
- **`rvw regress cosim --allow-sync mmio`**: DUT data for loads from declared MMIO regions (the Spike shim has no device state). Sync reasons are now checked from `recent_synchronizations`; a truncated history stays inconclusive.

Results (2026-11-13, `rv64imasu`, core `9f70315`): 4/4 C1 pass (MSIP and MTIP wake-up, MIE clear/set), 4/4 Spike match with `--allow-sync irq,mmio` (1–2 syncs each). Strict mode gives 1 match and 3 mismatches, all on `mtime` loads or asserted `mip` bits.

## Testing

- Native: `rvw regress run --project examples/vexiiriscv/rvw64-devices.toml --suite wfi-software-mie-0,... --rvfi-trace` and `rvw regress cosim ... --allow-sync irq,mmio` as above.

## PR 1016

[#1016](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/1016). Merged: 2026-11-13T11:42:21Z.

Title: feat(sec): run security checks on same-cycle memory buses

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
The third dry-run pass added U-mode and PMP to the independent RV32 core and ran `rvw sec isolation` and `rvw sec ift-core` on it. Three gaps blocked or misreported this.

1. **Same-cycle buses.** The native sec harness (`rtl.py`) supported only valid/ready buses with latency ≥ 1. A core with asynchronous RAM ports reads data in the cycle of its address, cannot wait, and has no `rsp_valid`/`cmd_ready`. Bus `latency: 0` now answers `rsp_data` (and its taint for IFT) from the current `cmd_address` in the drive step, queues nothing, and logs the handshake on `cmd_valid`. `rsp_valid` is optional there; `cmd_ready` is refused.
2. **Undocumented binding fields.** `rvw.sec.core_adapter` used `link` (default `../programs/link.ld`, the VexRiscv layout) and `march`, which the contract did not name. `docs/contracts/sec.md` now documents them and the latency-0 rule.
3. **Finding hidden as an error.** `ift-core --json` printed `status: violation` and exited 1; the CLI JSON fallback replaced that with `status: error, code: command_failed`. Exit 1 with a command's own JSON status now keeps the status and sets `verdict: fail`. Text-only output on exit 1 is still an error.

Roadmap notes: `rvw sec` now runs on cores with same-cycle memory ports. On the dry-run core (U-mode, 4 PMP entries): PMP isolation pair `no_leak_observed` (U-mode load of the denied keystore traps; RTL traces match Spike); IFT `ct-xor` `no_leak_observed`, `leak-index` violation on the data bus address at cycle 9.

## Testing
- `pytest rvw/tests/test_sec_core.py`: 9 passed (new: same-cycle drive, no queue, handshake log, IFT taint, missing `rsp_valid` refused for latency ≥ 1).
- `pytest rvw/tests/test_json_stdout.py -k finding_status`: passed (finding status kept; text failure still `command_failed`).
- Native on the dry-run core: `rvw sec isolation` (PMP pair) and `rvw sec ift-core` (two programs), results above.
- Fast set: 1939 passed, 1 skipped, 1 unrelated failure (`test_docs_site.py::test_docs_staging_does_not_write_sources`).
- Not run: full Python suite, VexRiscv sec reruns (their buses use latency 1 and the queued path is unchanged).

## Issues
Refs: #34. Cross-word accesses through a byte-addressed same-cycle data port need a project wrapper; the harness RAM is word-addressed.

Title: fix(memory): unblock full-program serialized hart replay

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
Fix serialized SMP bus ownership for complete programs. Keep one hart as owner while its requests retire, but allow that hart to issue later requests. Blocking all later requests can freeze the in-order pipeline before its previous memory operation retires. Other harts remain blocked until the owner's requests retire.

Add a complete shared-memory program with 128 AMO updates per hart, arithmetic, branches, a completion barrier and exact final-value checks. Replay each C2 retirement through the existing shared-memory Spike scheduler. Retain per-hart counts and fault controls.

Title: fix(uvm): check trap handler entry in the python cpu scoreboard

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary
The third dry-run pass ran native custom-core UVM for the first time: the pyuvm bench generated by `rvw uvm new` with the pass-2 project adapter, a project scenario, Verilator through `rvw regress cocotb`, and `CpuScoreboard` against a real captured Spike. Three generic defects stopped it:

1. **Handler entry refused.** RVFI sets `intr` on the first instruction of every trap handler, including synchronous traps. `CpuScoreboard` treated every `intr` record as an asynchronous interrupt, so any riscv-tests program (which ends with `ecall`) was refused at its first trap. Entry right after a retired trap is now checked like any retirement. `intr` without a preceding trap stays refused.
2. **Verilator lint stopped the build.** The cocotb worker built Verilator without `-Wno-fatal`; generated Spinal RTL has `UNSIGNED` constant-compare warnings and the build exited. Warnings still print; only errors stop it, as in the RiscvSim flow.
3. **No usable reference helper or diagnosis.** `spike_reference(platform_json, elf, work)` now builds the captured Spike instance the docs required. Mismatch messages name field, order, PC, instruction and both values (was only `SPIKE_MISMATCH:pc_next`).

Roadmap notes: native custom-core pyuvm on the dry-run RV32IM/U/PMP core passes against Spike: smoke (19 retirements), `rv32ui-p-add` (504, U-mode and traps), `rv32um-p-div` (135), a PMP-denied U-mode load (58). Open: the installed workstation venv is Python 3.15 and cocotb 2.1 supports at most 3.14, so the `pyuvm` extra needed a separate Python 3.14 environment.

## Testing
- `pytest rvw/tests/test_cpu_env.py`: 15 passed (new: handler entry after a trap checked, entry without a trap refused; `-Wno-fatal` build arguments).
- Native (Python 3.14 venv with `rvw[pyuvm,mcp]`, Verilator 5.049, Spike shim): the four runs above pass; before fix 2 the build failed, before fix 1 `rv32ui-p-add` was refused at its first handler entry.
- Fast set: 2063 passed, 1 skipped, 1 unrelated failure (`test_docs_site.py::test_docs_staging_does_not_write_sources`).
- Not run: SV UVM flow, full Python suite.

## Issues
Refs: #296. Asynchronous interrupts in the Python scoreboard still need an extended comparator.

Title: feat(vexii): serve plic stimulus mailboxes on rtl

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Wire the PLIC interrupt suites to VexiiRiscv RTL through the `rvw.stimulus/1` mailbox and the DeviceApiV1 plugin.

- **DeviceApiV1 ABI 2.** Appends `set_input(handle, input, level)` (for example a PLIC gateway source). Hosts (`DevicePlugin.h`, Scala `PluginDevice`) accept ABI 1 and 2 and read the new callback only for ABI 2. `PythonDevices.cpp` exports ABI 2 and maps it to `Device.set_level`.
- **`--stimulus-file` (RiscvSim, generic).** Loads `rvw.stimulus/1`; only adapters with `supportsStimulus` accept it. `StimulusMailbox` serves the next event when the program stores its step to `stimulus_step` and writes `stimulus_ack` after `settle_ticks`. C1 records `stimulus_file` (as given) and `stimulus_sha256`.
- **VexiiRiscv adapter.** Drives `plic-level` events through `DeviceBus.setInput("plic", ...)`. A passing program with unserved events becomes C1 `error`.
- **Selection.** Catalog rows `plic` (`device:plic`, MEIP) and `plic-delivery` (also SEIP and S mode); `rvw regress plan` now maps IRQ input 9 to `irq:seip`. `features64-devices.json` declares both; `prepare-suites.py` builds them; `rvw64-devices.toml` runs the 12 programs (build directories are `cache_paths`, so regress captures the stimulus files).
- **No unearned verdicts.** A strict mismatch at a load of the stimulus run's `stimulus_ack` word is reference-blind: `rvw regress privilege check` and `rvw regress cosim` report it as inconclusive with that reason (before: privilege check reported `fail`, "architectural mismatch").

Results (2026-11-13, `rv64imasu`): 12/12 PLIC programs pass C1 (priority, tie, threshold claim, contexts, gateway, enable changes; M and S delivery with global/local/threshold masking). Their claim-ID checks come from the independent PLIC model. Spike agrees for the first 56–61 instructions of each, up to the first mailbox read; comparison verdict: inconclusive (12).

## Testing

- Native: the 12 PLIC programs above; after the final rebase (main added `--sim-threads`), Scala `C2BackendSpec`/`WalkCaptureSpec`/`StimulusMailboxSpec` 11/11 and an RTL smoke (`plic-gateway`, `plic-delivery-s-1-global`, `wfi-software-mie-1`) 3/3 pass.
- Python: `test_standard_devices.py` (built library runs the ABI 2 `setInput` on a PLIC), `test_regress_suite_cosim.py` 21, `test_regress_applicability.py`, `test_privilege_scheduled.py` (reference-blind mailbox rule), PLIC/campaign tests 82 passed. Fast set: 1924 passed, 1 skipped. MCP list: no skipped tools.
- NOT RUN: a Spike reference that models the mailbox (needs single-hart external-write C2 events in cosim), the Python model-observation backend for `plic-delivery`, RV32 device profile.

## Issues

Refs: #84. Remaining: reference support for harness-written RAM (C2 external write events for one hart), RV32 CLINT/PLIC profile.

Roadmap notes: the stimulus mailbox and device input ABI let generated PLIC campaigns run on RTL; VexiiRiscv passes all 12 programs. The Spike comparison stays inconclusive at the mailbox word by design.

Title: feat(soc): boot the composed core from spi flash

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Add a read-only SPI NOR pin model and a real composed VexRiscv flash-boot example. The ROM stub reads the payload through the Spinal SPI controller, copies it into application RAM, checks a byte sum and jumps to RAM. Only the RAM payload reports success. Only the ROM ELF is preloaded. The generated RAM constructor and initial RAM observation exclude a hidden application preload.

Fix the legacy APB bridge for targets that omit PSLVERROR, as the Spinal SPI controller does. Full accesses return no error from such targets. Partial writes still fail before target select. A dedicated native smoke checks both paths.

## Testing

- Private source compile and composed elaboration passed with SpinalHDL 1.15.0 and the pinned private VexRiscv core.
- Unchanged payload: native cocotb test passed at seed 31; 5,150 CPU cycles, 573 retired instructions, 16 flash bytes, 20 SPI words, one flash transaction, finisher 1.
- Corrupted payload: deliberately failed the success expectation; 5,130 cycles, 569 retired instructions, finisher 3. The failure record is retained.
- RAM word zero was observed as zero before both runs. The positive run observed the expected payload word afterward.
- Existing SPI agent independently monitored the wire words.
- Flash model unit tests: 5 passed. Normal/fast reads, address restart, erased bytes, supplied identity/status, unsupported commands, missing identity and partial words are covered.
- LegacyErrorSmoke passed under Verilator assertions at seed 31.
- Fast set: 2,301 passed, 1 skipped, 8,316 deselected, 1 unrelated failure. `test_mcp_workflow_coverage.py::test_each_tool_has_a_profile_and_workflow` reports the existing `cov_probe_goals` MCP tool without a workflow entry. No coverage-tool or workflow files are changed here.
- Release hygiene: 40 passed.
- MCP listing has no skipped-tool errors.

Full Python/Scala suites, C1 gate acceptance, Spike co-simulation, physical flash, XIP, production bootloader behavior and program/erase modeling were NOT RUN.

## Issues

Refs: #1006, #1033

Roadmap notes: The composer can host a ROM-copy boot path on the real core, with the payload supplied only through the SPI pin model. Native positive/corruption evidence is recorded in the example README and integration guide. The NOR model is explicitly read-only. Hardware and complete boot qualification remain open.

Title: feat(cov): minimise measured suites and enforce smoke budgets

## Summary

Add `rvw cov smoke` and MCP `cov_smoke`. Use measured native point sets for exact cardinality minimisation through 20 tests. Use C1 wall costs and a declared startup allowance for greedy time-budget selection. Keep the full native denominator and historical point target separate.

Optional execution runs the recorded ELF/config/seed and coverage modes through project C1. A process deadline covers the lock wait, startup, build and programs. Timeouts cannot become pass because files exist. Conclusive C1 failures remain failures. New execution earns no coverage or strict reference credit.

| Core | Exact minimum in four measured tests | Budget selection | Historical point target covered | Native C1 elapsed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VexRiscv | 2 | 2 | 17915 of 17915 | 88.3 s |
| VexiiRiscv | 4 | 3 | 27644 of 27645 | 150.6 s |

Both runs passed all selected C1 programs under the 180-second deadline. The startup allowance was 120 seconds. VexiiRiscv leaves one previously observed point outside its budget selection. The exact minimum applies only to these measured signatures. It is not an optimum over arbitrary programs.

## Testing

- Final smoke, generated guide, MCP schema and effect checks: 94 passed. Includes deadline expiry after all result files exist and propagation of a conclusive C1 failure.
- Fast set after installing main's declared PyYAML development dependency: 2351 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed. Regenerated the agent guide to fix one failure; targeted checks now pass. The remaining `test_each_tool_has_a_profile_and_workflow` failure names `farm_observe`, an unrelated missing main workflow entry. No farm code or assertion was changed.
- Release hygiene: 40 passed.
- MCP discovery: no skipped modules or stderr.
- Native private-core C1 runs: 2 VexRiscv programs and 3 VexiiRiscv programs passed. Used `vex-dv`, `sbt-dv` and nice priority 10.
- NOT RUN: new Spike comparisons, full Python suite, BOOM, physical hardware, formal. The selected signatures come from the preceding strictly qualified coverage measurements.

## Issues

Refs: #349, #353

The time estimate does not guarantee runtime. The execution deadline enforces the adapter budget, with termination cleanup time as needed. Native point holes remain outside the observed-signature target. No C4 acceptance or new coverage credit is claimed.

## Roadmap notes

Record measured suite minimisation and deadline-bound C1 smoke execution on both examples. Keep exact minimum, greedy budget selection, historical signatures and fresh C1 outcomes distinct. Retain VexiiRiscv's one omitted observed point and all unhit native points.

Title: feat(arch): retain stores through bounded cache drain

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Retain committed stores in their existing shared store-queue slots until bounded FIFO cache acceptance. Start the cache write at drain. Pipeline hits at the configured width and block on additional refill delay. Forward loads from undrained stores, wait on partial overlap, and make fences wait for drain acceptance. Full queues stop rename. Commit uses the store slots already reserved at rename, with no second buffer allocation.

The positive width is opt-in. Zero preserves the earlier policy and native report parity. The measured region still ends at final retirement; it does not add final visibility time. ## PR 1238

[#1238](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/1238). Merged: 2026-11-13T16:17:45Z.

Title: feat(arch): bound memory retry window admission

Audit evidence label: ran on real core RTL.

## Summary

Add an opt-in long-response retry policy. Retain a missed load's compacting IQ line until response. Then reset its younger execution window, retain ROB/LSQ slots, and readmit through finite IQ capacity at rename width. Memory-order violations use the same bounded readmission queue. Recovery squashes active filler before it can block older retry admission. Recovery blocks correct-path issue while synthetic wrong-path work can finish until squash.

This is not exact probe-driven replay. Existing reschedule counters mix branches, traps and LSU causes. They do not identify the LSU reason or instruction window. No replay rate or penalty is fitted from those totals. Keep the existing five-cycle penalty and all base parameters fixed. Cache retries are limited to one per dynamic load. A long response may also include contention or translation. Exact typed replay remains open.

The README compares model retry counts with the mixed RTL totals without equating their predicates. Training absolute MAE rises from 7.33% to 9.46%; held-out MAE rises from 9.48% to 9.54%. The README and retained JSON record every paired delta, nonzero success count, same-step rank, and both absolute-error splits. No RTL run is repeated.

## Testing

Targeted timing, queue and retry tests: 41 passed. Tests cover missed-load retry, bounded readmission, queue pressure, retirement count, and required cache configuration. Final fast set: 2985 passed, 1 skipped, 8081 deselected. The saved multiply stream now retires fully in 38,020 model cycles under a 1,000-cycle progress check.

NOT RUN: new RTL or Spike runs, core builds, full Python suite, formal jobs, hardware, CI waits.

## Issues

Refs: #1047, #1098. Exact probe-driven LSU replay, typed reasons, nested speculation and physical accuracy remain open. This PR must not be treated as completion of exact replay qualification.

Roadmap notes: add bounded retry-window timing and preserve the missing typed RTL evidence as an open requirement.

A larger ROB could therefore change later branches' synthetic instruction mix. Index each dynamic branch into the frozen trace instead. Every variant now gets the same per-branch prefix. No variant-specific value or fitted parameter changes.

Add explicit `replay_window` selection for finite memory-order readmission without requiring a component cache. Preserve the earlier admission policy when both retry options are false, so mechanism ablation is explicit. Common recovery correctness fixes remain active for all policies.

Rerun the current-engine baseline and all three mechanism stages with the same base-only fitted parameters. Preserve the earlier per-stage results as historical `*-preseed-results.json`. Corrected calibration and delta reports share one engine. Exact typed LSU replay remains open.

## Testing

Targeted timing and filler tests: 42 passed. Added direct checks for a capacity-independent prefix, cache-independent memory-order window, and Boolean validation. The prefix test fails with the old cursor. All scores reuse saved RTL captures. Fast set: 2990 passed, 1 skipped, 8083 deselected, 1 warning. Focused pressure/dependence tests: 20 passed. Corrected baseline: 11/24 and 2/15 nonzero; occupancy: 15/24 and 6/15; drain: 15/24 and 6/15; cache-response retry: 10/24 and 1/15. The memory-order-only window score is also retained.

NOT RUN: new RTL or Spike runs, core builds, full Python suite, formal jobs, hardware, CI waits.

Refs: #1047, #1098. This removes an artificial sensitivity, not a new accuracy qualification.

Roadmap notes: use the corrected shared-engine study and retain all earlier scores as historical. Keep exact LSU evidence and structure-size qualification open.
